sentences.text: The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of a nearly complete fusion of the lower jaws. These jaws are toothless and fused frontally for about half their length, creating a distinct spearhead or arrowhead shape.
The lower jaws measure 29 cm long, and the estimated wingspan of the genus ranges from 3.5 to 4 meters.
In 2014, putative medullary bone-like tissue was reported from the mandibles of Bakonydraco, though researchers noted the specimens were skeletally immature.

Bakonydraco lived during the Late Cretaceous period in what is now western Hungary. The genus was named in 2005 by paleontologists Attila Ősi, David Weishampel, and Jianu Coralia. The type species is Bakonydraco galaczi, a name that honors Professor András Galácz. He assisted in the Iharkút Research Program where pterosaur fossils were first discovered in Hungary in 2000.
Researchers suggest Bakonydraco may have been a frugivore because its jaws are relatively tall and resemble those of Tapejara.
A 2025 analysis by Thomas and McDavid recovered Bakonydraco as an azhdarchid within the subfamily Quetzalcoatlinae.
Bakonydraco lived between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago during the Santonian stage.
The identity of the tissue in Bakonydraco is uncertain, with some suggesting it is vascularized endosteal bone and others suspecting it could be pathological.
